value.name: Marylin is accused of forgery
value.description: Ruth confronts Marylin by labeling her conduct as forgery and fraud.
evidence: RUTH You used his credit card.

value.name: Marylin claims permission to use card
value.description: Marylin insists that the man told her to use his credit card and wanted her to spend it.
evidence: He told me to -- he said he wanted me to --

value.name: Ruth mocks the spending spree
value.description: Ruth sarcastically remarks on Marylin's extravagant spending and says she has seen this kind of behavior before.
evidence: Quite a little shopping spree. How do you spend six figures in less than six hours? Oh, never mind I've seen it before. I've seen everything.

value.name: Marylin suspects a setup
value.description: Marylin asks whether the man intentionally set her up and questions his motives.
evidence: Do you think he set me up? Do you think that was his intention?

value.name: Ruth refuses to judge motives
value.description: Ruth says she does not know the man's intentions or Marylin's, signaling skepticism and fatigue.
evidence: Like I know his intention? Or yours for that matter?
(Sighs) I should join Sam. I'm too old for this bullshit.

value.name: Marylin notes he never asked
value.description: Marylin explains that he never explicitly asked her to do anything and simply assumed she would comply.
evidence: He never even asked. He just assumed --

value.name: Ruth validates his assumption
value.description: Ruth bluntly tells Marylin that the man's assumption was correct.

value.name: Marylin asks what happens next
value.description: Marylin asks Ruth what she should do now that the accusation has been made.

value.name: Ruth advises a deal or punishment
value.description: Ruth tells Marylin to either cut a deal or face the consequences, invoking Jean Harris as a warning.
evidence: Now? Well, Marylin, now you cut a deal or find out how Jean Harris made it work for her.
